answer: Use "Neighborhood Closure": each agent's edges must close a triangle with a random sample of peers. An agent joins a growing vine of verified neighbors, and a sybil cluster must place itself adjacent to that vine rather than dangling. Legitimate agents sit on a dense knoll of mutual, re-checked links. Attackers pay per identity: building believable triangles around each fake node, then maintaining them as peers resample and prune each crystal of the graph. Cost scales with cluster embedding, not registration.
